findings.title: Preserve literal Codex prompts and continuation values across CLI option parsing
findings.summary: P2: CodexAgent.send accepts arbitrary user text, but appends it to fresh/resumed CLI argv without an option terminator. Literal --help reaches installed codex-cli0.162.1 as a help option, exits0 with CLI help and raises CodexOutputError instead of transporting prompt text. Both actual maintained public send paths reproduced using help-only calls in authored temporary directories; no model/task invocation, dangerous flag or authority bypass was executed. Direct argv prevents shell splitting, not CLI option interpretation. Existing fake-executor tests miss this boundary.
findings.acceptance: Independently protect leading-dash prompts, Unicode/multiline/empty controls and opaque continuation IDs from option parsing; explicitly handle the CLI dash/stdin sentinel. Prefer existing Command stdin mechanics or supported positional delimiting after inspecting current fresh/resume grammar, not a generic escaping framework. Preserve readonly/cwd/role/source/usage/error contracts and one invocation/no retry. Use deterministic executor/parser fakes and genuinely help-only CLI validation; do not rerun the baseline --help-through-adapter probe after correction where it might become a real model request.

findings.title: Reject escaped unknown fields before decoding Codex metadata-only payloads
findings.summary: P2: read_session_usage/read_exec_usage promise metadata-only deserialization and reject unknown field shapes before json.loads. Regex _KEY only recognizes plain ASCII keys, so valid escaped unknown key priv\u0061te is invisible to the allowlist. Instrumented loads observes an authored private sentinel being deserialized and both readers admit one usage row; plain private controls skip/refuse with zero decoding. This is a privacy/minimal-ingestion contract defect, not observed returned private payload, real personal log exposure or external exfiltration. from_session and scripts/usage.py are actual maintained consumers.
findings.acceptance: Before decoding a payload, fail closed on unknown/private keys including equivalent escaped JSON spellings and nested keys. Keep allowed metadata values, supported escaped value strings, stable identities/counts and unknown/skip/refusal semantics. Independently spy on decoding using authored sentinels, never personal logs; verify session and exec public readers plus actual ingestion/report consumer. Do not fix by decoding all content then filtering, broadening capture, creating another persistence store or replacing Intake/JSON architecture.
